> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/security.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/security.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **150** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 69aa630b9fd6ef20f76cbac9ed4d9b9efa69c804` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f7c7a36c0b6ac2173a74543c1ef614f7984c722c` — the merge of head `1267e3cb2b5cec5d538fd5da7401a68bd0adde78` into base `69aa630b9fd6ef20f76cbac9ed4d9b9efa69c804`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f7c7a36c0b6ac2173a74543c1ef614f7984c722c && git checkout f7c7a36c0b6ac2173a74543c1ef614f7984c722c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 69aa630b9fd6ef20f76cbac9ed4d9b9efa69c804 1267e3cb2b5cec5d538fd5da7401a68bd0adde78 && git checkout -B drift-repro 69aa630b9fd6ef20f76cbac9ed4d9b9efa69c804 && git merge --no-ff 1267e3cb2b5cec5d538fd5da7401a68bd0adde78

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 69aa630b9fd6ef20f76cbac9ed4d9b9efa69c804
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 69aa630b9fd6ef20f76cbac9ed4d9b9efa69c804` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1267e3cb2b5cec5d538fd5da7401a68bd0adde78`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/security/permission.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts, packages/spec/api-surface/security.json, packages/spec/export-origins/security.json, packages/spec/src/security/permission.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/runtime-authoring-gate.hierarchy-scope.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.runtime-authoring-gate.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-explain-access.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-read-verdict-inputs.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/showcase-scope-depth-fallback.dogfood.test.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/plugin.ts, packages/core/src/kernel.ts, packages/core/src/kernel-base.ts, packages/core/src/lite-kernel.ts, packages/core/src/plugin-loader.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-service.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/sharing-service.ts, packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/stack-refusal-envelopes.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/index.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/showcase-scope-depth.dogfood.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/showcase-scope-depth-write.dogfood.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/federated-phantom-share-grant.dogfood.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/admin-platform-admin-standing.dogfood.test.ts, examples/app-showcase/src/security/permission-sets.ts, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, .changeset/26188-hierarchy-scope-without-resolver.md (prose face)

Read on the net diff `origin/main...origin/pr-26305` (merge base `617f27eb`), 16 files, 555+/36-. Inputs: card #26188 and all three comments, ruling `6416233738` and item reading `6415971852` on #26059, os-dev-report `6426008287`, PR body and file list, the head's 41 check-runs.

### ① Derived judgments

**Public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged.**

1. `@objectstack/spec/security` gains the export `findHierarchyScopeGrants(permissionSets: unknown)`. Pure, tolerant of any input, no Zod schema touched; `api-surface/security.json` and `export-origins/security.json` each gain exactly the one matching row. The claim allowed one spec export of the existing helper; this is it. **Right.** The `stack-refusal-envelopes.test.ts` pin is a verbatim fragment (`uses readScope='unit_and_below', a HIERARCHY scope`), not the whole sentence, so byte-identity of `defineStack`'s text is a reading, not a pin: compared line for line, the old inline loop and the new `${g.finding}. ` + the two unchanged tail fragments produce the same string (same array guard, same `objects` guard, same key order, same `HIER` set, `String(ps?.name ?? '?')` equals the template's coercion). **Byte-identical; right.** `findHierarchyScopeGrants` is a sound single source: one list, one sentence, both doors append their own remedy.
2. `@objectstack/plugin-security`: `ExplainEngineDeps` (a public type export, `index.ts:88`) gains the optional member `hierarchyResolverMounted`, an optional function returning boolean. Absent reads as before. **Right**, and correctly declared as a widening.
3. `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`: two new exports from `runtime-authoring-gate.ts` (`HIERARCHY_SCOPE_CAPABILITY_REQUIRED`, `HIERARCHY_SCOPE_RESOLVER_SERVICE`) and `findHierarchyScopeCapabilityGaps`; `evaluateRuntimeAuthoringGate` gains the optional `hierarchyResolverMounted` argument; `AuthoringGateHost` gains the same member. All additive. **Right.** One note: the service name is spelled a fourth time as a string literal (the sharing plugin, the explain wiring and `spec/contracts/sharing-service.ts` prose each spell `'hierarchy-scope-resolver'` by hand); the new constant is not read by the sharing plugin. Not a defect, see ③.

**Accept-set change (the narrowing), bounded exactly.**

- What is refused: a write whose singular type is `permission` only (`args.type !== 'permission'` returns early; the `object` draft test pins it), whose body carries `readScope` or `writeScope` equal to one of `own_and_reports`, `unit`, `unit_and_below` (both axes, each depth, pinned by the 3x2 loop), on a write with `state: 'active'`, when `hierarchyResolverMounted === false`. `own` and `org` are untouched. One `issues[]` entry per grant, located at `permissions.NAME.objects.OBJECT.readScope|writeScope`, inside the gate's existing 422 `INVALID_METADATA` envelope under rule `hierarchy-scope-capability-required`. **Right, and inside the ruling** (9a: "refuse on publish").
- Which doors: `assertRuntimeAuthoringRules` is the one body all four reach. Direct active save (`saveMetaItem`, protocol.ts:21167); per-item publish and the package batch publish both go through `promoteDraftForPublish` (:22918, called at :22512 and :23957); restore goes through `refuseRestoredBodyTheSaveDoorRefuses` with `state: 'active'` (protocol-authoring-gate.ts:131). **Four doors, one rule, right.**
- Restore-to-version: refused too. This is not a new door the PR invented: "a restore refuses what the save door refuses" is the standing invariant of `refuseRestoredBodyTheSaveDoorRefuses` (#25467 cut 8), and re-activating a stored version that carries an unenforceable grant would make the same inert declaration live. The card names `PUT` and `publish` as the measured doors and asks that "the runtime path match" `defineStack`; a restore is a runtime activation. **Within the ruling's shape; right.** Restore carries no advisories (its receipt declares none), so a restore of a draft-state version hears nothing; drafts are not restored to active, so nothing is lost.
- Draft save: the draft branch of both `assertRuntimeAuthoringRules` and `evaluateRuntimeAuthoringGate` returns the same finding at `severity: 'warning'`, `error: null`; `saveMetaItem` attaches a non-empty `advisories` array to the 2xx regardless of mode (:21590). The branch reads no collection and no stored row (the `migrate-stored` pass still returns `[]` first). **Consistent with D1**: no rule gates a draft; a draft now hears one warning. The gate's own D1 comment was updated to say so. **Right.**
- Host with no service registry: `hierarchyResolverMounted()` answers `undefined` only when `getServicesRegistry` is absent on the protocol (a direct construction) or the lookup throws; the gate judges nothing on `undefined` (pinned). Through `MetadataProtocolPlugin` (plugin.ts:249) the registry is always a function; on a kernel whose context lacks `getServices` it answers `new Map()`, which reads as `false`. Both in-repo kernels (`ObjectKernel`, and `LiteKernel` via `kernel-base`) expose `getServices()` as a copy of a plain `Map` (`kernel-base.ts:130`, `kernel.ts:319`), so every in-repo production host is judged, and the `undefined` reading is the exact shape `rlsMembershipResolverKeys` already has. **Left unjudged on purpose, and the purpose holds**: `defineStack` is that host's door. The PR body's "the CLI" phrasing is looser than the code (the CLI's `os serve` boots a kernel and is judged; what is unjudged is a protocol built without a registry), but the behaviour is right.
- Can a deployment WITH an enterprise resolver be refused? Not by any in-repo path. The protocol reads `ctx.getServices()`, a snapshot of `kernel.services`; `kernel.registerService` writes that map and the loader (`kernel.ts:383-388`), which is how the reference resolvers in the dogfood worlds register. The sharing plugin reads `ctx.getService('hierarchy-scope-resolver')` (`sharing-plugin.ts:690`), a three-tier lookup (services map, then the loader's instances, then factories). The two agree for a `registerService`-registered resolver. They would disagree for a resolver registered through `registerServiceFactory` and not yet resolved once (it sits in the loader only until the first `ctx.getService` caches it): the protocol would read "absent" while sharing enforces it. No in-repo plugin registers any service by factory, the enterprise plugin lives in cloud and is not readable from here, and `rlsMembershipResolverKeys` and the SDUI-manifest read carry the identical exposure today. **Judged: the PR's "same lookup the sharing plugin uses" is overstated (same name, not same resolution), the practical answer is no, and the residue is a pre-existing shape; recorded as a ③ flag, not a defect of this PR.**
- Resolver mounted: `true` returns `[]` on both states (pinned, pure and through a real registry). **Nothing changes; right.**
- `package-author` channel: `assertRuntimeAuthoringRules` still returns `[]` before the draft branch, so a package-author write hears neither the warning nor the refusal. That is the gate's standing posture (package authoring is judged by `os build` / `defineStack`, where this grant is already refused), and the ruling's door is the environment save door. **Right, unchanged, noted in ③.**

**`INVALID_METADATA` with `rule: 'hierarchy-scope-capability-required'` and the ADR-0112 ledger.** The ledger's unit is the code, and provenance is per emitting package: `INVALID_METADATA` is already registered under `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` (ledger line 673, inside the 653-723 block), so a new rule id inside its existing `issues[]` envelope adds no stamp site the provenance gate (`check:error-code-provenance`) would sweep and no row is owed. Reusing `STACK_HIERARCHY_SCOPE_CAPABILITY_REQUIRED` at an HTTP door would have been a new emitter of a `door: 'none'` spec code (line 1574, the `defineStack` family comment "where a throw aborts before any HTTP boundary exists"), owed a metadata-protocol row in the file this claim keeps off. The card's acceptance line ("either reused or a new row; the PR names which") is met: the PR names the reuse and says why. **Correctly outside the ledger's requirement; right.** A rule id is a `RuntimeAuthoringIssue.rule` string, the key a renderer groups by, not a wire code.

**Explain (9b).** The new arm sits after `ownerIsMe` and after `depthAdmitsRow` and before the `sharingMatches === false` arm (explain-engine.ts:2096-2110), guarded by `depthScope !== 'org'` (the `!depthWidens` arm above already caught `own`, so only hierarchy depths reach it) and `deps.hierarchyResolverMounted?.() === false`. `depthAdmitsRow` requires `sharingMatches === true && !ownerIsMe && !anyShareAdmits && (org || sharingFilter !== null)`, so **a row the depth really admitted is never reported as resolver-absent**. Outcome `excluded` when the owner-match failed, `not_evaluated` when the row got in some other way. The wiring reads `resolveKernelService('hierarchy-scope-resolver') != null` per explain, kernel-side, and the real-stack harness now registers its stub under that kernel name and hands the sharing service the same lookup, which is the honest fixture. **Right.** One corner is worded wrong, not misattributed: a hierarchy depth on an object whose sharing filter is `null` (no owner column, a bypass object) on a resolver-less runtime now lands in the new arm with `sharingMatches === true` (the matcher admits a `null` filter) and `anyShareAdmits === false`, and the detail ends "a share admits this record (see the sharing layer)", where before the PR the `sharingFilter === null` arm said "the sharing service imposes no owner-match on this object". The outcome (`not_evaluated`) is right; the sentence is not. Reaching it needs a stored hierarchy grant on an ownerless object on an open-edition runtime, a row the door now refuses to create. Recorded in ③ as a follow-up, not blocking.

**Shipped examples, apps and dogfood worlds.** Read every world that declares a hierarchy depth: `showcase-scope-depth` (`bootScopeWorld('unit', false)`) and `showcase-scope-depth-write` (`withResolver: false`) deliver their profile through `bootShowcase({ defaultPermissionSets })`, the SecurityPlugin catalog, never the metadata door, so the gate does not run there; `federated-phantom-share-grant` drives `sharing.checkEdit` with a context `__writeScope`, no metadata write; `admin-platform-admin-standing` only mentions the scope in prose. `authz-conformance.matrix.ts` names the depth as a matrix id. `examples/app-showcase` deliberately authors no hierarchy depth (`permission-sets.ts:131-137`: "this open example does not author them"). The only world that PUT a hierarchy grant through `/meta/permission` with no resolver was `showcase-scope-depth-fallback`, and the dev's full battery at `4cf2c1a5` measured exactly that one failure. The fix at `1267e3cb` is test-only, pins the 422 + rule through the real HTTP door first, then saves with the reference resolver mounted and unmounts it from both stores (`kernel.services` and `pluginLoader.serviceInstances`, consistent with the kernel's two-tier `getService`), so the fail-closed read is still proven against a stored row. **No shipped example, app or world is newly refused; the one affected world is fixed honestly.** The tests claimed (7 pure, 3 door rows, 2 explain cells, 1 real-stack cell, 2 spec rows, 4/4 dogfood) are all present in the diff, and the three ablation legs each name the line that would go red.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/26188-hierarchy-scope-without-resolver.md`: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: patch`, `@objectstack/plugin-security: patch`, `@objectstack/spec: patch`. `Metadata-protocol: none` is the right kind: `PermissionSetSchema` parses exactly what it parsed before, no authorable key, value or default moves; the refusal is a runtime-gate rule conditional on a deployment fact, the class the #6285 and #21476 rules belong to. Under ruling A the level follows the kind alone, so `none` takes `patch` on all three. (A reading of "a value refused" as `narrowed` would require `minor` on metadata-protocol; I resolve it for the PR because the protocol an author writes against is unchanged, and the gate's own rule reads `narrowed` as a contradiction only beside a missing `(narrowing)` arm.) **Right.**
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing: on a runtime with no hierarchy resolver, … ; widened: …)` on both the PR body and the changeset. Through `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` the value reads `yes` and `readArmToken` reads `narrowing` (the arm regex accepts the word followed by `:`, which is neither a word character nor `|`); the rest of the parenthetical is the seat's argument and is ignored. That is the documented combination "`yes (narrowing)`: a diff that widens one surface and narrows another. Both facts are true and both are read." The spelling is what the repo's rules and the Check Changeset gate expect for a narrowing that also widens; the claim's provisional `no (narrowing)` was rightly revised, since a `no` would have denied the spec export. **Right.**
- BREAKING: the `(narrowing)` arm is BREAKING, so a banner and an ADR-0087 disposition are owed. Present: a `**BREAKING**` banner with Before / Now / Fix; the title and the changeset summary carry the `!` (`fix(metadata-protocol)!:`); exactly one adr-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, a category in `CATEGORIES`. The body carries no FROM→TO label, no rewrite arrow and no framed migration section, so the prescription detector has nothing to refuse, and the exemption is honest: the author's repair is a choice between a non-hierarchy depth and an enterprise runtime, which no ledger entry can derive. `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` runs inside the `Check Changeset` job (pr-automation.yml:999), which concluded `success` on this head. **Owed and present; right.**
- No `authorable-surface/` or `authorable-defaults/` baseline moves; `api-surface` and `export-origins` rows are the only spec artifacts owed for a function export, and both are present.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Dev deviation: `Clause-②: yes (narrowing…)` instead of the provisional `no (narrowing)`.** Accepted, see ②. The spec export and the public `ExplainEngineDeps` member are real widenings.
2. **Dev deviation: two harnesses changed beyond the new cells.** `explain-read-verdict-inputs.test.ts` moving its stub resolver into the kernel service map is a correction (the old harness gave the sharing service a resolver the kernel never knew, which is exactly the contradiction 9b is about). The dogfood world's rework is judged in ①. Accepted.
3. **Acceptance note 1: `SaveMetaItemResponseSchema.advisories` `.describe()` left stale.** Read at protocol.zod.ts:1064-1076: "applied to this body on its way to `active`" is now partly stale, since a draft save can carry this one warning. The key's shape and the invariant that matters to a consumer ("every entry has `severity` `warning` or `info`", "present only when at least one advisory was raised") still hold, and the text is description only. Accepted as a one-line docs-only follow-up on `packages/spec`, outside this claim's one-spec-change allowance. Not blocking.
4. **Acceptance note 2: the object-level depth layer (no record) is unchanged.** The ruling names `explain-engine.ts:2040-2075`, the record cell.
